parts.title: A Hundred Years
parts.text: Ms. Alvarez's class had one big job: fill a time capsule for the school's hundredth birthday. First, Yolanda, Hugh, and Saanvi explored the school **archive**, a dusty room full of old yearbooks and photographs. Hugh stretched a long **timeline** across the wall to show every big event, from the first graduating class to the new library. Saanvi was amazed by how much each **era** had changed the school, from chalkboards to tablets. "This is our school's **legacy**," Ms. Alvarez said. "It is everything earlier students passed down to us."

parts.title: Treasures from Home
parts.text: That weekend, each student searched at home for something to include. Yolanda found a brass compass, an **antique** that had belonged to her great-grandfather. Saanvi brought a **vintage** record from the 1970s, still in its cardboard sleeve. Hugh's grandmother loved to **reminisce**, so she told stories for an hour before handing him a ticket stub, a **memento** of the first football game she ever attended. Saanvi also tucked in a silver locket, a **keepsake** from her aunt.

parts.title: Sealing the Capsule
parts.text: On sealing day, the class gathered around a steel box. Each student wrote a letter, and Yolanda used an engraving pen to **inscribe** all their names on the lid. They hoped that a future **generation** of students would open the box in fifty years. "In **retrospect**," Hugh said, "this project showed us that ordinary things become history."

parts.title: The Stone Vault
parts.text: As the capsule was lowered into its stone vault, Yolanda smiled. Someday, strangers would hold their treasures and wonder who they were. She hoped those readers would feel like friends, just as she had felt friendship in the old photographs.

On a rainy Saturday, Dario climbed into the attic with his grandmother to sort through an old trunk. "This room is like a private _(1)_ where our family keeps its old records," she said. "Every box holds a piece of our family's _(2)_."

Inside he found a copper kettle, a true _(3)_ more than a hundred years old. Beside it lay a _(4)_ hat with a velvet ribbon, the kind that was stylish in the 1950s. A tiny silver thimble was a _(5)_ from her own mother, and a faded ticket was a _(6)_ of the first movie she ever saw.

Grandma loved to _(7)_ about the town where she grew up. She had once used a nail to _(8)_ her initials inside a table drawer. Each _(9)_ in the family had left a mark somewhere in the house. Dario drew a _(10)_ showing the biggest events from every decade. "Every _(11)_ in history, from the horse-and-buggy days to the space age, has taught us something," she said. "In _(12)_, this attic was the best classroom I ever had."
